newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-More options seen in Australia-NZ air talks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-More options seen in Australia-NZ air talks.

text.p: The tie-up between Air New Zealand Ltd and Ansett Airlines Ltd had given the two countries a golden opportunity for talks over Air NZ's plans to seek rights to fly through Australia to other destinations, Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said on Friday.

"In a sense this commercial transaction gives us a golden opportunity for the development of beyond rights between Australia and New Zealand," Sharp said after giving a speech to the aviation press club here.
Air New Zealand bought a 50 percent stake in Ansett from TNT Ltd in September for about A$475 million.

"It is interesting that the marriage between Air New Zealand and Ansett gives us more flexibility and more options in the way we go about negotiating beyond rights between Australia and New Zealand," Sharp said on Friday.
"We gave a commitment to the New Zealand government that we would negotiate beyond rights and we will," Sharp said.
"Australia and New Zealand have still to consider the issue of beyond rights," he said.
"The government will take its decisions on this matter against the normal background of assessing the overall benefits that such rights might bring to the Australian economy."
A Transport ministers conference is due to held in Australia on November 15.

The single aviation market agreement which comes into force on Friday was signed in September, almost two years after the previous Labor government suddenly scrapped an earlier agreement just days before it was due to take effect.

The new agreement allows Australian and New Zealand airlines to fly within and between both countries without restriction, but there are still limits on flying across the Tasman and on to a third destination.
Air NZ has been lobbying for more Australian landing rights in order to better tap into the lucrative Asian markets, a move against which Qantas Airways Ltd has been battling.
The original single aviation agreement between the two countries included an extension of beyond rights.

The shock move, which soured Australian and New Zealand relations in the face of the Closer Economic Relations agreement, was blamed on the Keating government bowing to pressure to protect the price of the then state-owned Qantas ahead of its public share float last year.
